prospect.name: Michael Hogan

prospect.training_background: Two years back into consistent training after a period of slipping. signals: Already training consistently and eating whole foods — this is an upgrade, not a rescue
Explicit good-to-great framing: 'my bar was here, and then my bar was here, and now my bar is going here' and 'I want to be like the absolute best version of myself that I can be'
Treats the price as a market-normal signal rather than a shock: 'I know that's how much a lot of coaches are charging'
Already buys coaching in another domain — he retains a business coach

Departs from the pure optimizer in that his blocker was capacity rather than conviction: 'whether I'm committed to partnering with a coach for six months and pay this kind of money and actually gain the full benefit, I'm not 100% sure'

goals.text: Lose body fat, particularly around the gut, and get leaner
Be very athletic — able to surf, skateboard and snowboard well
Better mobility and less morning stiffness in back, knees and shoulders
Snowboard without worrying about falling and getting hurt
Build muscle mass ahead of the testosterone decline he expects between 45 and 50
A plan he does not have to think about — 'I don't want to think about what am I going to do today, what am I going to eat today'
Get protein from about 100g to 150g a day
Model fitness for his children — 'I tell them, I have to exercise, I have to work out, and you need to too'

pains.text: Back, knee and shoulder stiffness at 5/10, worst in the mornings
Calisthenics leaves him feeling limber but without power — 'I need more pump, like I need something to lift weights, but I don't want to lift weights'
Severely time-constrained — five children at home over the summer, a business, and a business coach whose requests he already cannot meet
Fears signing up and not being able to follow through, so wasting the money — 'I'm paying the money and I'm not getting out of the program what I'm putting in'
A couple of glasses of wine every day which he believes is driving his body fat
Protein intake short of his own target — getting 100g, wants 150g
Knows that at 45 a couple of skipped weeks compounds — 'start skipping a workout, start skipping a couple weeks, it slips, slips'
Has previously slipped into complacency and gone downhill; is wary of it recurring

objections.raw_quote: if it was just me, and I knew my heart, like we started this program that I could give 100% time wise... I know I have a tendency to like, want to start something and then I'm not able to like, follow through 100%. And I'm like paying the money and I'm not getting out of the program what I'm putting in.
objections.rep_response: Agreed with the objection rather than working it, and built a downsell around it — 'How about this? We get just started with something that's a little bit more self-based' until the children return to school

objections.raw_quote: I don't know if I'm necessarily... I don't know if I'm ready to invest $1,000 a month, necessarily, but I know that's how much a lot of coaches are charging.
objections.rep_response: Did not isolate or work the objection; asked what was coming up for him and, once timing surfaced, moved to the $1,000 tier

objections.raw_quote: I'm not like 100% sure about, you know, I need to think about it for a minute. But I'm open to it. And I'd like to revisit this.
objections.rep_response: Asked what was mainly coming up for him and identified the time commitment as the real blocker — a good diagnostic move

objections.raw_quote: I'm feeling a lot of pressure for the one-on-one right now. I don't want to add, I'm trying to have good growth without adding too much pressure.
objections.rep_response: Accepted it and confirmed the self-serve route as the lower-pressure option. Proposed label: 'accountability_reads_as_pressure' — the programme's core differentiator being experienced as a cost rather than a benefit.

evidence: Clear verbal agreement to the $1,000 self-serve tier: 'Well, I'm definitely, I'm very interested in that. I could definitely see myself doing that'
Asked for the link himself — 'Can you send me like an email link or something?' — and confirmed 'Perfect. Yeah, let's do that'
Committed to completing it same day: 'when do you think you're going to be able to complete that?' — 'Sometime today.'

Counter-evidence and the reason this is not scored as closed: no payment link was actually sent during the call. The rep said he would send one afterwards by WhatsApp — 'I can send you a message with the sign-up link and then just let me know when you've done that' — so the verbal-agreement-plus-link-sent rule is not satisfied on the evidence in this recording.
Counter-evidence: the prospect ended the call abruptly to meet his wife before work, and no payment, agreement or onboarding step was completed
This is a genuine boundary case and may well resolve as a $1,000 close within hours; it should be reconciled against the payment processor rather than left to the transcript
outcome.next_step: Rep sends the self-serve sign-up link by WhatsApp; prospect intends to complete it the same day and message back

notable.note: First transcript in the corpus to name the DH setter — 'I already heard a couple of things from Derek.' Two process findings. The rep had a verbal yes on the $1,000 tier and let the prospect leave the call without collecting payment or sending the link live. And the timing objection, which was the actual blocker and was stated three separate times, was never worked: the rep agreed with it and sold a cheaper product around it, which is the opposite of the OD play. Also, the twelve-month option was raised in answer to a direct request to 'break down the different investment options' and its price was never stated.
